chunks: And Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And to Allah is the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to find thereto a way.' He said: 'He sets out walking if he has nothing.' I said: 'If he cannot walk?' He said: 'He walks and rides.' I said: 'If he cannot do that?' He said: 'He serves the people and sets out with them.'
ai.seo_question: What are the different levels of ability required to perform Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to clarify the gradations of financial and physical capacity (istita'ah) required for Hajj, emphasizing that the obligation is flexible and inclusive. The hierarchy—walking, then riding, then serving as a caravan attendant—demonstrates the Shia scholarly view that even those with minimal resources can fulfill the duty through labor, ensuring no one is excluded due to poverty.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2504 - Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked him about the verse of Allah (swt), the Exalted: "And [due] to Allah (swt) from the people is a pilgrimage to the House—whoever is able to find thereto a way" (Surah Aal-E-Imran 3:97).
Imam (as) replied: "He should set out on foot if he has nothing."
I said: "What if he cannot walk?"
Imam (as) said: "Then he should walk and ride."
I said: "What if he cannot do that either?"
Imam (as) said: "Then he should serve the group and set out with them."
